case_name: Shyamal Kumar Sen vs Mrs Sanjukta Mukherjee And Another
facts_of_case: The case involves the family of Paramesh Chandra Sen, who retired from government service. His son Shyamal left for England in 1966. The family had rental income from an ancestral property. Tragedy struck when the youngest daughter died in a road accident.

legal_principles.principle: The rules of evidence are not technical; they are, in essence, rules of common sense that are rooted to the principles of natural justice.
legal_principles.held: If Shyamal did not have a chance to question how Debjani or her Advocate came to be in possession of the purported affidavit, the court could never have applied Section 90 of the Evidence Act to invoke the principle of presumption embodied therein without the condition as to custody being complied with.

legal_principles.principle: It is for the executor to dispel the suspicious circumstances leading to the execution of a Will.
legal_principles.held: The principle recognised in the judgment reported at AIR 1968 SC 1332 (Gorantla Thataiah v. Thotakura Venkata Subbaiah) was noticed for the proposition that it is for the executor to dispel the suspicious circumstances leading to the execution of a Will.
cited_cases: AIR 1968 SC 1332 (Gorantla Thataiah v. Thotakura Venkata Subbaiah)
